newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government sets fees for mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government sets fees for mobile phones.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government announced on Wednesday a range of charges for private cellular telephone service operators, fixing the fee for licence holders at Z$1.5 million (U.S.$137,000) annually.

In a statement, the government said in addition to the licence fee, operators would be charged Z$20,000 (U.S.$1,830) for each channel in which they operate as well as five percent of their net operating revenue.
The fees would remain constant for three years but there might be increases after a review by the information, posts and telecommunications minister.

"Connection fees and tariffs to the public switched network, the ordinary PTC (state-owned Posts and Telecommunications Corporation) phone system, will be agreed between the licence holder and the PTC," it said.
Agreements between private operators and the PTC would however have to be approved by the minister.
The announcement follows a government invitation two weeks ago to potential cellular phone operators to tender for the country's first private cellular phone network.

The tender invitation came just before a January 14 deadline set by the supreme court for the government to outline specifications for the cellular telephone operators after a private local company charged that government delays in granting it a licence were aimed at frustrating its business.
The PTC launched its own mobile cellular phone service last September.
